```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r DBConnect}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/midwest_airbnb_extended.db")
listings     = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
availability = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "availability_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
reviews      = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "reviews_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```


## Task 1
```{r Task1}
# Who owns the market. Count listings per host_id across all three cities and join the count back to the listings. Report how many hosts have 10 or more listings [A1], and what percent of Chicago's listings those hosts hold [A2].

count = listings |> 
  dplyr::group_by(host_id) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    num = dplyr::n()
  ) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(num))

count

ten_or_more = count |> 
  dplyr::filter(num >= 10)

nrow(ten_or_more)

listings_with_count = listings |> 
  dplyr::left_join(count, by = "host_id")

chicago_ten_or_more = listings_with_count |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    city == "Chicago",
    num >= 10
  )

nrow(chicago_ten_or_more) / nrow(listings |> dplyr::filter(city == "Chicago"))

```



## Task 2
```{r Task2}
# Value for a family of four. Keep entire homes (room_type == "Entire home/apt") that sleep at least 4 (accommodates >= 4), have at least 10 reviews, and a rating of at least 4.8. Add price_per_person = price / accommodates, take the median per city and neighbourhood, and keep only neighbourhoods with at least 20 such listings. Report the Columbus neighbourhood with the lowest median price per person [A3].

sorted = listings |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    accommodates >= 4,
    number_of_reviews >= 10,
    review_scores_rating >= 4.8
  ) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    price_per_person = price / accommodates
  )

sorted = sorted |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city, neighbourhood) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price_per_person = median(price_per_person),
    num_listings = dplyr::n()
  )

sorted = sorted |> 
  dplyr::filter(num_listings >= 20)

sorted

columbus = sorted |> 
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus") |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(median_price_per_person))

columbus
  

```

## Task 3
```{r Task3}
# What earns. By city and room type, compute the median price, reviews_per_month, and estimated_revenue_l365d in one summarize call, using dplyr::across() and skipping NAs. Report the median estimated revenue of Twin Cities entire homes [A4].

earnings = listings |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city, room_type) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(
      c(price, reviews_per_month, estimated_revenue_l365d),
      ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )

earnings

twin_cities = earnings |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    city == "Twin Cities",
    room_type == "Entire home/apt"
  )

twin_cities
```

## Task 4
```{r Task4}
# Concentration. Within each city, sort listings by estimated_revenue_l365d, largest first, and mark the top 10 percent (the cutoff is ceiling(0.10 * dplyr::n()) rows). Report the percent of Columbus's total estimated revenue earned by its top 10 percent [A5].
top_ten = listings |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(estimated_revenue_l365d)
  ) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    cutoff = ceiling(0.10 * dplyr::n()),
    rank = dplyr::row_number(),
    top_10 = rank <= cutoff
  )

top_ten

columbus = top_ten |> 
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus")

total_sum = sum(
  listings |> 
    dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus") |> 
    dplyr::pull(estimated_revenue_l365d),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

sum(
  columbus$estimated_revenue_l365d[columbus$top_10],
  na.rm = TRUE
) / total_sum

```

# Task 5
```{r Task5}
# The year ahead. Join the October 2026 rows of availability (month == "2026-10") to the entire-home listings. Call a listing mostly taken when nights_available < 0.5 * nights_in_month. Report the city with the lowest share of mostly-taken entire homes [A6] and that share [A7].
october = availability |> 
  dplyr::filter(month == "2026-10") |> 
  dplyr::inner_join(
    listings |> 
      dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt"),
    by = "id"
  )

october

october = october |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    mostly_taken = nights_available < 0.5 * nights_in_month
  )

october

shares = october |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    share = mean(mostly_taken, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(share)

shares

```

# Task 6
```{r Task6}
# Demand by season. Join reviews to the listings, keep July 2025 through June 2026, and total the reviews per city and month. Report the Twin Cities' busiest month [A8] and the ratio of its busiest month to its quietest [A9].

demand = reviews |> 
  dplyr::inner_join(
    listings,
    by = "id"
  ) |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    month >= "2025-07",
    month <= "2026-06"
  )

demand = demand |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city, month) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    total_reviews = dplyr::n(),
  )

demand


twin_cities = demand |> 
  dplyr::filter(city == "Twin Cities") |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total_reviews))

twin_cities

ratio = max(twin_cities$total_reviews) / min(twin_cities$total_reviews)
ratio
```

# Task 7
```{r task7}
# The Superhost premium. Among entire homes with a known host_is_superhost ("t" or "f", not NA), compute the median price and median rating for superhosts and for other hosts in each city. The premium is the superhost median price minus the other-host median price, in dollars. You report the three premiums in your answer to B1.

superhost = listings |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    !is.na(host_is_superhost)
  ) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city, host_is_superhost) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rating = median(review_scores_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
  )

superhost

```


# Task 8
```{r task8}
# What the join lost. Use dplyr::anti_join() to count the listings that have no rows in availability [A10], and say in your README which city loses the most.

missing = listings |> 
  dplyr::anti_join(
    availability,
    by = "id"
  )

nrow(missing)

missing_city = missing |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    missing_count = dplyr::n(),
  ) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(missing_count))

missing_city


```
